subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should plugin or externally registered recurring agent-turn cron jobs default to disabled/pending approval unless an operator explicitly enables them, and which cost/quota guardrails should be solved in this issue versus #14376 and #42475?
rationale: Current code proves the risk, but choosing default enablement, model-warning policy, and quota-enforcement ownership changes operator workflow and plugin API expectations.

options.title: Require operator approval for external recurring agent-turn jobs
options.body: Make plugin or third-party recurring agent-turn jobs pending/disabled by default, add operator enablement and model/cost warnings, and split gateway budget/circuit-breaker work to the existing related issues.

options.title: Keep auto-enable but add warnings and dry-run summaries
options.body: Preserve existing auto-start behavior while surfacing inherited model, interval, and estimated call-count warnings in update/doctor flows.

options.title: Split and close this umbrella
options.body: Move consent, cron retry policy, provenance, and gateway budget work into separate canonical issues, accepting that no single issue tracks the combined user harm.

recommendation.title: Require operator approval for external recurring agent-turn jobs
recommendation.body: Make plugin or third-party recurring agent-turn jobs pending/disabled by default, add operator enablement and model/cost warnings, and split gateway budget/circuit-breaker work to the existing related issues.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main cron and plugin scheduled-turn implementation history points to vincentkoc as the closest routing owner for the policy decision.
